notes.title: Magnus Lore Reveal #39 Humbird
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34489002/68b92202217bf23ed1a7b8415b904efd89b9fc2e.png[/img]

Spirits of Wind and Song, the Guardians over the Sands, and the Protectors of Everdust are just some of the names that we have found from the dusty old tomes in the Library. All of these refer to the humble humbird, and all of its grown incarnations. Although it may not seem it now, the Humbird was one of the most populous Magnus in all of the Everdust. Filling homes, accompanying travellers and flying free under the Everdust Sun, the Humbirds dominated the local landscape with its soft breezes and amazing arias.

The ancient societies of the Everdust held the Humbird with very high regard. In the old desert kingdoms, killing a Humbird is seen as a crime which normally led to harsh and often brutal punishment. The bow wielding nobles and the elite of the Old Everdust would normally have a Humbird as their companion. As a pet or a hunting partner, their owners would usually get very attached to the humbird often spending more time with it compared to other people. Such was the standing of the Humbird during the Everdust’s Golden Age.

The Humbird has two forms that it can mature into, those being the Hymnbird and the Gustbird. The Hymnbird is a master at controlling the healing winds, being able to close even the deepest cuts and mend bones by simply using wind magic. The Gustbird on the other hand uses wind magic for a much more destructive purpose. Unlike the soft feathers on the Hymnbird, the Gustbird has razor sharp feathers that can slice with terrifying effectiveness. They both make wonderful companions, but stay away from the sharp bits.

Head Librarian,
Figaro

notes.title: Magnus Lore Reveal #38 Skreetle
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34489002/47f8bb9deae4543055fa48ad252cc41232fa1be2.png[/img]

All magnus were spawned from the Tree of Origins, that is the lore that has been passed down for generations in Ethia. Our understanding of creation stems from the mythology of the Goddess and her fight against the demons. But when left to question, the Librarians pondered, what truly is life and where does it come from. Is life an energy, or an element like fire and ice? Maybe the answer can be found from the humble Skreetle over in the Ruined Kingdom.

The Skreetle are an anomaly, a remnant of what once was, and the keepers of the Old Kingdom in an unfortunate way. When first setting eyes on a Skreetle, its most apparent feature would be the bright, luminescent, green sacs around their claws and abdomen. These sacs are not filled with venom or poison as was first theorized, but with the materialized essence of life energy itself. Touching the fluid like substance will heal the gravest of wounds and can even heal the sick.

As bizarre as it sounds, the Skreetle actually attacks by injecting life energies into its target. With an appropriate amount, this would actually heal whomever was injected, but when injected with too much, it would destroy the integrity of the target’s body. We know that the Old Kingdom was a bastion to a bounty of nature and life seem to spring from the ground itself. Perhaps the Skreetle is a reflection of those days, or perhaps all the life in the land was taken to fill those bright green sacs.

Head Librarian,
Figaro

notes.title: Magnus Lore Reveal #34 Pander
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34489002/8988af4a0b5aca9c3f22a60bb362f3c36a7fe781.png[/img]

When discussing about Magnus, it is not unusual to assume that we are talking about wild creatures that live in simple and natural habitats. There are only a few Magnus that are classified to have sapience, at least from the ones that have been discovered and recorded by the Library. The Blipking on Vokka Island is one example of a sapient magnus, and also Busterina the famous Bushbrawler musician. There is however one species of Magnus that has created a whole community and civilization of their own, the Pander.

Panders live in the mountains of the Frigid Tundra, relatively isolated and protected from most of the cold. The Panders have built a society around the prophecy of the coming doom, readying themselves for the End that is to Come. A Pander’s life is filled with training and growth, each Pander will be allowed to choose which path it wishes to take and it eventually leads to different evolutions when the time comes. The three distinct paths of the Pander ultimately teaches the same principles, strength and discipline will allow the Pander race to escape from Doom.

Despite having a unified goal the three paths of the Pander have three different versions of the prophecy and when asked would say that theirs is the legitimate and true version of the prophecy. The Library is not able to find much in terms of evidence to support each path’s claims, nor could we find the origins of the prophecy in the historical and archeological findings in the Tundra. Despite their constant squabbling, the Panders were able to build an advanced settlement and an organized society, which is truly a great achievement.

Head Librarian,
Figaro

notes.title: Magnus Lore Reveal #32 Seirun
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34489002/ff1243343d028d02436aa4b5249b6ef185cfebbe.png[/img]

Translucent ribbons flitting through the Tundral skies, shimmering in sunlight and glimmering in moonlight, an absolutely breathtaking sight to behold. The Seiruns have long been considered the most beautiful Magnus’ (apart from the Valemer) by scholars and naturalists of Ethia. Not only are they masters of navigating through the skies, but they move just as nimbly through the icy cold waters of the Frigid Tundra. 

Seiruns are observed to have 2 different paths for evolution, the high-flying Seirel and the grounded Seiron. Both these evolutions primarily feed underwater, and usually sup on the underwater vegetation. The cold waters of the Tundra is at the perfect temperature for Ballonions to thrive, which the Seiruns seem particularly partial to. When diving into Tundral waters, it is common to see Seiruns of all kinds coiling around the Ballonions while nibbling on the fruit.

The Seirun is able to use it’s body to bend light and use it as a tool for scaring off predators and attackers. Attacked Seiruns are usually seen dispersing cones of concentrated light into the eyes of their enemies, which normally result in the unfortunate creature being blinded and then taken apart by their intended quarry. In legend, the Seirellius and Seironius are considered to be the “Bringer of Storms” and “Bringer of Cold” respectively, and is used to explain why the Tundra is constantly covered by a blanket of Snow and Ice.

Head Librarian,
Figaro

notes.title: Magnus Lore Reveal #31 Budthorn
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34489002/c151945ca457e7f8d39a7246da3c4ba744d6c271.png[/img]

Traversing the dunes of the Everdust, it is not uncommon for one to come across various species of cacti thriving throughout the bone dry desert. However, one should always be aware of a certain magnus that looks remarkably similar to the other unsuspicious cactus. The Budthorn lies in wait above the sand, posing still as its prey gets closer and strikes when it is already too late for its target to escape. 

The Budthorn has the ability to shoot its needles out at quite a distance, there has been stories of travellers in caravans that were hit unsuspectingly by a barrage of needles and were unable to see where the attacks were coming from. The same cannot be said with the evolutions of the Budthorn, both the Cacthorn and Dualthorn lose their ability to shoot their spike but instead gains the more terrifying ability to rapidly grow their spikes underground to impale their targets.

All Budthorns have the ability to absorb energy from the Sun, using it as temporary sustenance or as a battery to charge their beam attacks. The two head of the Dualthorn are surmised to have their own intelligences and act independently from each other, though we are unsure who or how they control their shared body. Observation of the Dualthorn shows that the two heads can get antagonistic with each other, sometimes even resulting in one head pulling off the other.

Head Librarian,
Figaro

notes.title: Magnus Lore Reveal #30 Bunsnub
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34489002/8563674ee28ccc2bd49ed8fc75e4599085d0ed1e.png[/img]

Hiding beneath the snowscapes of the Frigid Tundra, a curious little magnus hides itself from the rest of the world. Bunsnubs are magnus local to the cold and unforgiving tundra, constantly burrowing into the solid cold earth with relative ease. When first trying to observe them, it was quite the challenge to pick out the Bunsnub from all the snow on the ground. The colour of the Bunsnub camouflages it very well, and its ability to not move for long periods of time further contributes to the difficulty of spotting it.

The first contact with the Bunsnub was rather uneventful, they are extremely passive creatures that would not even budge even when approached by my expedition team. We were puzzled at their lack of acknowledgement, since they did not appear to be predators and were much rather the opposite. The Bunsnubs would also not enter their shells,  but rather would lie on their bellies even when angrier looking magnus appeared.

The piece of the puzzle was the extreme resilience of the Bunsnub’s anatomy and the array of unique skills that help it to survive in the harsh conditions. Not only does the shell block most attacks, the fur of the Bunsnub also provides incredible protection to its body. The Bunsnub is also able to release extremely cold winds that slows and sometimes immobilizes their attacker, giving it ample chance to escape or attack. Attack a Bunsub only when you have adequately high attack power, or not at all.

Head Librarian,
Figaro

notes.title: Magnus Lore Reveal #29 Dunepup
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34489002/d00002eb8bede21a35656988cbb879b73d35bd1f.png[/img]

The Howl beyond the Dunes, the Blur in the Sands, many travellers to the Everdust would have encountered the Dunehounds during their trek across the desert. Such encounters, though frequent, should be avoided at all cost. The Dunehounds are known to be extremely aggressive and would attack human caravans no matter its size. A single Dunepooch would be troublesome to deal with, however they usually hunt together in packs along with the older members. 

Observing the Dunepups in their habitat was a dangerous endeavour, sneaking did little to mask our scent from the Dunehound’s keen sense of smell. We were fortunate enough to find a vantage point that allowed us to look down into a Dunewolf’s den. The Dunepups were observed playing among each other whilst being protected by the larger Dunewolves. There were times when a Dunepup would sneak past a Dunewolf and follow a hunting pack, but then they would swiftly be sent back once discovered.

The hunting tactic of the Dunehounds is to hit hard and hit fast, they were observed to dash straight into their target and attack with fang and claw. The howls of the Dunehound also have a mind-altering quality that usually throws their victims into disarray. Survivors of the Dunehound attacks would tell us that they would be filled with anger and resentment whenever hearing the howls up close, though the reliability of said information is questionable at best.

Head Librarian,
Figaro

notes.title: Magnus Lore Reveal #28 Saggithorn
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34489002/271ad6dc45b9cb793d35e2f8115bd5c7481c45d0.png[/img]

It’s no mystery why the Frigid Tundra is named as such, with the constant torrent of snow and ice all year long, it leaves a lot to be desired in the warmth department. The local populace of Penguins are able to withstand the cold temperatures and many of the magnus on the island actually require the cold weather to live comfortably in their habitat. There is however one Magnus that thrives on warmth, the Saggithorn, and it achieves it in a rather amusing way.

Wandering through the Tundra, there often are times when you can feel a warm (or at least far less cold) wind blowing, and most of the time you can find a Saggithorn nearby. These magnus will release heat from their own bodies in order to create a warm area around it. It would seem that scales on their back are responsible for permeating heat into the air. The green on their scales are actually little plants like moss that cling onto them for warmth and protection.

If you are planning on travelling through the Frigid Tundra, it would be wise to bring along a Saggithorn. Sleeping in the cold for nights on end will do untold damage to an adventurer’s psyche and having a warm friend to rest upon certainly doesn’t hurt. The Saggithorn is also really passive, which means that it won’t attack you despite having some serious looking spikes on their tail. Just make sure not to bother them too much while they are sleeping. 

Head Librarian,
Figaro

notes.title: Magnus Lore Reveal #26 Shime
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34489002/e2776d511ca318689d5f6526cd103f4f61d48f62.png[/img]

The Frigid Tundra is a dangerous place to traverse through, both explorers and residents alike are subjected to unrelenting winds and subzero temperatures. It is not uncommon for one to claim seeing phantasms in the day or wild visions of beasts in the night. If you strain your ears and listen closely, you can almost hear a soft melody of bells and chimes whenever in the Tundra, you would be forgiven for assuming it a hallucination but in fact it is simply the Magnus, Shime.

The Shime are a peculiar bunch of magnus that grows natural musical bells and instruments on their body. The Library is unsure whether the Shime is mimicking the instruments that it has seen before, or if our human instruments are in fact imitations of the Shime’s physiology. The music of the Shime has a two-fold effect, it can both aid and harm the listener depending on the intention of the Shime. There are testimonies of explorers having different reactions to the same song of the Shime.

My personal encounter with the Shime is quite uneventful. During our trek towards the elevated areas of the Tundra, my party came across a group of wondering Shime clinking and ringing in the air. We stayed quite a distance away from them until one of my party was brave enough to approach quietly. When he came about a couple of yards away, the Shimes immediately bunched together in a defensive position, a constant ring permeating the air. We backed down quite hurriedly and took another path up the mountain.

Head Librarian,
Figaro

notes.title: Magnus Lore Reveal #25 Sarvillion
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34489002/b41ee74604ac2db1e3a99983b7e1c0c604ace749.png[/img]

The Everdust is a harsh mistress, the dry near endless sands of the dunes provide little in terms of protection and sustenance. Anything living outside of the Oasis are subjected to near unbearable living conditions, but the crafty creatures of the Everdust have found ways to combat this environmental disadvantage. One such creature is the Sarvillion, an armored magnus that hides under the desert sands.

Sarvillions start of its life as a quadruped, the heavy scales on its back weigh it down and its upper body has not developed enough strength to carry the load. This however works as an advantage to the sarvillion as it protects the vulnerable areas of its back. As the Sarvillion matures, it learns to move upright and its arms also develop drastically to the point where it has one of the strongest arms in all of Ethia. 

Energy is hard to come by in the Everdust, most creatures scrape through by doing little or getting food from unconventional sources. The Sarvillions however, supplements their energy by harvesting the one resource that is abundant in the Everdust, sunlight. The scorching rays of the Sun are absorbed through the Sarvillion’s back plates and can be used to sustain the Sarvillion and also for fending off competition or attackers. The Sarvillion is able to survive for weeks without eating just as long as there is a healthy amount of Sun on its back.

Head Librarian,
Figaro

notes.title: Magnus Lore Reveal #24 Harpri
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34489002/7136e218447809433b33c04c01ca04756abd0bd2.png[/img]

How trustworthy is the word of weary sailors? Especially those that have to brave the frigid waters of the Tundras. Tales of giant sea monsters, unnaturally moving waters, and beautiful birdlike maidens calling them to shore. It turns out that the whole story about maidens are actually true, and we currently know them as the Harpris. Settling by the edge of the Tundral waters, they charm passing ships and travellers into their watery graves.

When first setting eyes upon the Harpri, the only thing that came to mind was how beautiful it was. It turns out that the Harpri has the natural ability to charm any creature, man, beast or goblin will not be able to resist this impulse. This is all before it starts to sing, the melodies that are produced by the Harpri rivals even the best vocalists that I know all around Ethia. The sweet melodies will soothe your soul and relax your nerves, truly terrifying.

There have been rumors floating around that some researchers have been doing experiments with the Harpri and a terrible creature has emerged because of it. A dark twisted version of a Harpreen has been sighted by locals, but there has so far been no concrete proof of such a creature existing. I hope to be able to dispel these rumors the next time I visit the Tundra, the thought of meeting such a creature sends shivers down my spine.

Head Librarian,
Figaro

notes.title: Magnus Lore Reveal #23 Momochi
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34489002/e439bda45a2ae4f0dcb364f2dd13705978af0d91.png[/img]

Following the survey of the Coastal Vokka Island and the Forests of the Wilkwoods, I once again return to the home of the Library, the Great Everdust Desert. As you may have guessed, the magnus here in the Everdust have been studied and scrutinized by the members of the Library a great deal more compared to the ones in other regions. Despite this, there are still magnus that stump researchers even to this day, for example the Momochi.

How can something so cute exist? There is no doubt that the Momochi at any point of its evolution is incredibly cute. It defies the pattern of evolution of almost all other magnus, but one would not put off the chance to cuddle with a Daimochi even if we know that it will crush an adult human just with its weight. Another point that befuddles us is the transition of black horn to gold horn for the Daimochi, there seems to be no purpose or cause for this change but it occurs nonetheless.

Living so close to water within a cave in the Oasis, the Momochi’s primary diet source is actually fish. It helps them to maintain a healthy layer of fat below their fur, which helps them to defend themselves from attackers. The hide of the Momochi is surprisingly tough, which makes them one of the best defenders in all of the Everdust. But only savages will attack a Momochi, no one in their right mind would ever hurt something so adorable. 

Head Librarian,
Figaro

notes.title: Magnus Lore Reveal #22 Windhorn
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34489002/2b088b13173ef60e492f961ded808e902648d31e.png[/img]

The pursuit of understanding Magnus evolution has been a constant study to the members of the Great Library.  Conventional wisdom will tell you that a Magnus will evolve into forms that are closely related to its predecessor or environment, but there is one Magnus that stumps even the greatest of Librarians. The Windhorn hails from the deep forests of the Wilkwoods, and its evolutions vary wildly from each other, sporting a multitude of elements.

Fire, Earth and Life, these are the categories that the Great Library has split the different evolutions. It would seem that each line of the evolution, exemplifies the paragon of each said element. According to local legend, the Windhorn are the spirits or even the will of the forest itself, and represent the different ways or powers of the Wilkwoods itself. The Furyhorn represents destruction and change, the Hardhord represents stability and protection, and the Greenhorn represents life and growth.

The same local tribes also have tales of a creature, which will only appear when the Wilkwoods are in dire straits, which is the collective will or the whole of the forest’s spirit. The mighty Tritanhorn, causing tremors with each step, burning all matter of life around itself, and destroying all invaders that would harm the forest. So far there is no evidence of this creature ever existing, but the insistence of the locals begin to waver my resistance to such theories.

Head Librarian,
Figaro

notes.title: Magnus Lore Reveal #21 Dreadclaw
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34489002/255b471f72ad87d47e716b26762c9fbf61db7dfc.png[/img]

The Terror of the Deep, the Ancient Fury, the Clawed One, records from the Library have not been kind to the Guardian of the Coastal Island of Vokka. Though the moniker of Dreadclaw doesn’t help to improve its image any more than the legends of savagery and uncontrollable rage. Among all the guardians of Ethia, the Dreadclaw may be the least known and most avoided by scholars, mostly due to its reputation but also its relatively secluded and hostile habitat may have contributed to the difficulty of research.

It is known that the Dreadclaw was once worshiped by the denizens of Ethia, its stone temple still stands hidden within Vokka Island. According to Library records, it was once the patron god of fishing, hunting and feasts, however all worship for the Dreadclaw came to an abrupt end. The scholarly community has debated and deliberated the cause of this occurrence, but it still remains a mystery to us all.

My personal expedition to the Dreadclaw’s temple was a fruitless attempt much like most of my contemporaries before me. The abandoned temple was infested with dangerous fauna that snapped and attacked any trespassers, not only that, ancient machinations were controlling the access to the inner sanctums of the Temple. Unless you are a brave adventurer or an expert in ancient architecture, I would suggest that you abandon your quest to study the Dreadclaw.

Head Librarian,
Figaro

notes.title: Magnus Lore Reveal #20 Wilker
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34489002/90339349e427bdd54ae7b91701e7f8ffb6ec5084.png[/img]

Within the woods that bears its namesake, the Wilker stands silently as the Guardian of the Forest Island. Known throughout history as a mild mannered and passive entity, many travel far to offer reverence towards the majestic Wilker. In recent years, the Wilker roams the woods less and less, and prefers the seclusion of the heart of the forest rather than the boisterous outer woods. Lucky adventurers will still bump into the Wilker and may receive its powerful blessing.

According to local legend, the Wilker is the Mother of all Trees, which birthed every variety of plant on Ethia. We know that the Forest is undoubtedly connected to the WIlker, but even until now we are unable to determine where the Wilker ends and the forest begins. Some believe that the entire forest is actually the Wilker and the entity we see is simply a manifestation of the Wilker’s will or power. I highly doubt this, as it is not consistent with the other Guardians of Ethia.

While certainly known to be mild and passive, there are stories that depict a fighting Wilker crushing those that intend to harm the Wilkwoods or its inhabitants. Personally I was able to catch a silhouette of what seemed to be a walking tree, though it vanished before I could get a good look. The infestation of thorns could not have come at a worst time, I would have to return to the Wilkwoods one day and speak to the Wilker myself.

Head Librarian,
Figaro

notes.title: Magnus Lore Reveal #19 Vale
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34489002/4a84ccdfea118c6a97fc4f2efac011b9b0ba156c.png[/img]

Lying across the Coastal beaches of Vokka, the Vales are truly an anomaly even when compared to other weird Magnus. Found mostly lying on their side, they seem to subsist mainly by picking of whatever they can find on the ground. Their distinct purple hue and passive nature makes them prime targets for other predators to feast upon, but the natural strength of the Vale’s tail generally deters such occurrences. They are one of the magnus that remarkably look like fish, but definitely do not have the ability to swim.

Metamorphosis of the Vale has stumped the researchers of the Library ever since their discovery. The fact that a fully piscine looking Valevale, will turn into the semi-humanoid Valemer or Valephyr still baffles the greatest minds of Ethia. Surprisingly the outer appearance of masculinity and femininity of the Valemer and Valephyr does not determine the gender of the creature. Female Valemers have been observed bearing young, to that I can attest to.

Despite the irregularity of the Vale’s evolution pattern, there is no cause for the people of Ethia to panic. Most of the Vale are passive in nature and do not bother travellers and onlookers, Valemers will only attack when one of their own is being assaulted, so I would suggest not poking a Vale (at least when a Valemer is around). To conclude the piece, there is no reason to worry about the Vale, unless there’s an ancient civilization that feared the Vale enough to carve a giant stone statue of a Valemer, but what are the odds of that.

Head Librarian,
Figaro

notes.title: Magnus Lore Reveal #18 Oriton
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34489002/011dfc3b972e802070ab039e154367ab210b4d21.png[/img]

The tribal traditions of the Wilkwood natives may seem weird to most of us in the Library and perhaps even Ethia as a whole. If one would venture deep enough and find remote parts of the Wilkwoods, traces of the Old religion can still be found in carvings, murals and sometimes people. The Oriton is deeply tied to the tales of the Old Sky God, sometimes being portrayed as guardians and at other times destroyers.

The Old tradition thought of the Oriton as gifts from the Lightning Spirits that served the Sky God. The crystals that embed themselves into the Oriton’s body emit strong lightning power when used and making tools from it imbues it with powerful lightning energies. Many tales speak of the Gods calling upon the Oriton to be instruments of their will, but whether it be aid or harm, the Oritons terrible violence will end the tale with bloodshed.

Observation of the Oriton shows two distinct branches of physical maturity, one being the quadrupedal Ceraton and the bipedal Kiloton. Notable difference in the Oriton’s diet can be observed between the two, the ones that eventually become Ceratons can be seen munching on Silver ore while the other can be observed in shallow waters catching fish to eat. If the Old stories are anything to go by, it is best if one does not approach these ancient beast lest one wishes to incur their wrath.

Head Librarian,
Figaro

notes.title: Magnus Lore Reveal #17 Blip
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34489002/105bed37078641715a8954ae8d668c0cfd418cc2.png[/img]

The coasts of Vokka are populated by a translucent, jelly-like Magnus known as the Blip. They are often seen floating sandy areas which are generally near the sea. Contact with them is usually uneventful as they are one of the most docile Magnus that you can find on Ethia. There is not much research being done on the Blip, apart from a particularly zealous librarian that I shall refrain from naming. The information below shall be from the writing of this librarian, therefore should be considered at best pure speculation.

Blips first appear to be herbivores, or at least vegetation is important for their bodily growth. With thorough testing, it appears that Blips can consume almost anything but whether it contributes any nutrition remains to be observed. The blip lacks any sort of defensive layer to protect against attacks, but the secret to their resilience would be an especially potent healing magic that closes wounds at an astounding rate.

As the Blips grow and mature, they would grow antennae at the top of their heads. It seems that this allows them to communicate with each other telepathically, thus forming somewhat of a hivemind among the blip population. This would explain their extremely defensive nature, as well as how they know when one of their brethren is being attacked at quite a distance away. I wonder if we can tap into the wavelength of their communication and join in on their collective. There is no magnus more magnificent than the illustrious Blips.

Head Librarian,
Figaro

notes.title: Magnus Lore Reveal #16 Duskel
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34489002/9ee8c4998aca80fd8d08ae5b0d54a559f09952a4.png[/img]

The Magnus of the Wilkwoods are inexorably linked to the Forest itself, so much so that many of them are considered Forest Spirits by the locals and scholars alike. Duskels are unmistakably fauna, however interestingly they exhibit many properties of flora in its anatomy. Disregarding the leaves that grow on their chests as they mature, Duskels are able to collect energy from sunlight using the large yellow plates on their backs.

When it was first discovered that Duskels had this capability to absorb sunlight, scholars from the Library were quick to hypothesis what exactly was the use of such a feature. Was it to use as sustenance? Regulate body heat? Or maybe to fire giant lasers from their antlers? The answer came when on of the researchers accidentally scared a young duskel which prompted its older kin to step in and fire solar rays at the unfortunate Librarians. 

Another interesting feature of the Duskel are the hard growths over the front of their face, which turned out to be part of its skeleton. The green film over their eyes allows it to have a better view in the dark and the hard bone like exterior allows it to headbutt with enormous strength. Library records of the Duskel are extensive and plentiful, mostly due to the massive curiosity over the back plate solar energy debate, and there was no need for further observation.

Head Librarian,
Figaro

notes.title: Magnus Lore Reveal #15 Moota
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34489002/68e82e0dd694f28df8797e7e7dfe08b5cca8ea04.png[/img]

Records of Magnus and their origins have been vague from the very beginning, the oldest records state that Magnus were created by the Goddess Aquila during the end of the Old War. When the Tree of Life was fragmented to save Ethia from its invaders, the Magnus sprang from the life energies of the broken splinters or so the records say. Magnus were born from the very land of Ethia itself, and this would explain why all of them exist as terrestrial creatures despite what convention would say.

The Moota is one such creature that baffles our scholars, with what seems to be a tail fin at its lower end and other piscine like feature around its body. The Moota exists exclusively on land despite this, and does not even venture close to water, consuming land vegetation for sustenance. The only thing that links them to water are the projectiles that they can conjure, deadly icicles that pierce through armor. This has caused scholars to speculate if the form of the magnus is simply elemental expression given life.

The Mootas of Vokka Island have considerable strength and aptitude in magic, but they generally don’t attack and remain passive towards goblins and newcomers. Speaking to the local people, Mootas provide a bounty of nutritious milk and tales of the most delicious Golden Milk certainly brings roaring jubilation to the crowd. It is nice to see Goblins, Humans and Magnus coexisting and being merry, it is certainly a nice diversion from the other ferocious and dangerous magnus.

Head Librarian,
Figaro

notes.title: Magnus Lore Reveal #14 Fangmist
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34489002/fcec1f51c0d538515c23bd1352bb9ffd6c34b2aa.png[/img]

The Fog of the Wilkwoods hides many terrors, all of them will send shivers down your spine, but none more so than the Fangmist swarm. Navigating through the dense fog, these creatures will kill anything that it considers a threat to the hive, though they rarely consume their victims. Most Fangmist live in service to their Queen, acting as extensions of the Queen’s will and carrying out all orders without question. 

Any adventurers that are thinking of exploring the Wilkwoods will need to prepare for the unfortunate event of the Fangmist’s poisonous sting. Fangmists have the ability to fire poisonous projectiles at incredible ranges, so one should not feel at ease just because you are not able to see the creature. It is said that the Fangmist’s poison is one of the most potent in the land of Ethia, and simply having skin contact with a Spearmist’s poisonous attack renders one to be in incredible pain.

Remarkably, the main component of a Fangmist’s diet actually consists of honey and nectar collected from the flora of the Deep Wilkwoods. On rare occasions, Fangmists can be seen near water trying to spear for fish. It seems that the consumption of fish is vital for the growth of the Fangmist, but they do it only when they are at the stages close to their transition. The Library is fiercely interested in the honey that these Fangmist produce, but would caution all  collectors to be wary of these insectoid nightmares.

Head Librarian,
Figaro

notes.title: Happy New Year & A Letter From Us!
notes.notes:
Hey guys! Happy New Year and it’s 2020! How’s your New Year Celebration? We hope that it’s all going great! It has been a very meaningful and adventurous year for us in Magnus Games Studio. We’ve learnt a lot of things throughout the years but 2019 was an extraordinary year for us. We would like to say thank you to all of you who have supported Re:Legend from the beginning of the development.

For a new game studio, it was challenging to create the game we wanted because the team was small at the beginning and it takes time for each individual to grow and blend into the environment. It was you who supported us through Kickstarter, it was you who pushed us to learn, it was you who taught us to adapt, it was you who made us grow. We kept solving as many things as we could on a daily basis. It was you who motivates us to keep making Re:Legend a better game. We never felt that failure was an option because we knew we have the responsibility to complete the game, and ship it with all the things that we have promised.

Few months ago, Re:Legend’s Early Access was released on Steam and it was infested with bugs and we sincerely apologize for the unpleasant experience. But because of the rough launch, we’ve found so many things that we could improve upon. We have decided to rework the core experience, which is the multiplayer and most of the early days scripts where they were not optimized. From the player’s perspective, there might not be much changes in terms of  visuals, but we’ve reworked many of systems to make sure that it runs smoother as we go. While we are reworking the system, it might clash with the legacy structure so it will take some time to sort out the stability of the game. At the same time, we will collect all your feedback and analyse them and improve as much as we could.

We know that a lot of you are frustrated and are asking questions like:“How hard it is to fix such a small thing?”, or “Are they really working on the game?”. But behind the facade of a game, lies a team of developers with real life problems and challenges. It is heartbreaking to see that some of our team members had to work even when their family members are in the hospital, or even when they themselves are sick yet they are still giving their all. We can never expect everyone to understand what we are going through in the studio or what are we working on simultaneously as we’ve only posted updates once a month. In reality, there are many more things that has happened other than the things that we have announced. To make things clearer for the future, we are looking at having a development roadmap such as Trello or something similar so that you guys can see what we’re working on at all times.

Other than the development, we do have some great things going on for the studio as well. One of it is that we have a newborn baby programmer in the house during early access launch! One of our programmers gave birth to a healthy little baby and everyone was excited and happy about it because this is the first baby that the studio ever had and nobody knows how to take care of one. We were even joking about taming him as a Magnus. ( Disclaimer: No baby was harmed in the process ) Other than that, seeing the game being globally ranked 1 during launch and being the popular game of September on Steam puts a smile on our faces too. Not to mention Re:Legend was even on the list of “ The best release of 2019“! We really appreciate every small thing that has happened and do not forget to celebrate them because we know that there will be a long road ahead of us. We know that you will be walking along with us through this amazing journey.

This is a heartfelt letter from us to you and we hope that all of you will be healthy and happy while gaming throughout 2020 and for many years to come! Once again, thank you to all of you who have always been supportive and motivated us along the way. For to those who have given us a down-vote, we are truly sorry about that and we will work hard and hopefully turn it into an up-vote in the future! We have a very clear vision and planning for 2020 and we can’t wait to share more about them with you guys soon! Once again, Happy New Year! #2020

See you in-game, Tamers of the Land of Ethia!

-Magnus Games Studio

notes.title: Re:Legend - Multiplayer Guide
notes.notes:
Greetings tamers! 

For today, here's a small guide to help all tamers access the multiplayer mode in Re:Legend! We hope everyone can try it out and play with your friends! We made multiple improvements towards our multiplayer system and are striving to improve the game everyday!

How to join multiplayer in Re:Legend ?

Currently with the rework in Re:Legend, the multiplayer is now integrated into the game rather than a selection in the menu. 

There are a few simple requirements and steps to access multiplayer within the game.

[olist]
[*] Both players need to be at the quest part “Blips Vs Prunis” to unlock the multiplayer counter in the Guildhouse. It is part of the first string of tutorial quests introduced to the player. We made it required as players will need to get their starter items and tools before venturing out to meet other players.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34489002/4773b3030aff159d40efdb7c2da7aaae5a53edaf.png[/img]

[*] Multiplayer requires your internet connection and Steam to be logged in ( with your friends online as well!) With your Steam on and friends added, let's head into Re:Legend.

[*] The host (or the save file you want to play together) should head into the Guildhouse in Vokka Town. (It is beside the Hospital where you started)
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34489002/77c4feb84e85097a7879ef18eca0c4dc614e2539.png[/img]

notes.title: Major Patch: New Biome Unlocked! The Everdust Desert is coming to you!!
notes.notes:
Greeting Tamers, the Version 16 major content update is finally here! The theme of this update is Desert, and with it brings a lot of new content and fixes to the game. As we welcome the shiny and new, sadly we need to say goodbye to the old. With this update, all old save files from before the update will no longer be usable, this would mean that all progress is effectively wiped and everyone will need to start fresh.

We understand the frustration of the save wipe, but with the full rework of many systems in the game, the old save files were hard to recover. We hope that with the fresh start with the new systems will prevent any previous bugs that was and will happen with old save files. We take this into heavy consideration, but to safeguard from future save wipes we decide to do it earlier than later. We will keep this to a minimum and prevent doing save wipes after this one. So go and venture forth with full force!

New Content contains:
 
[list]

[*][Biome] The Everdust Desert is a harsh and unforgiving land that features over 6 distinct zones and over 30 areas to explore. 
[*][Story/Quest] Continue your journey into the Everdust Desert to find out more about your lost memory and explore the secrets of this land.
[*][World Travel] Multiple new islands to explore each with their own hidden treasures waiting to be discovered.
[*][Magnus] Over half a dozen new Magnus and their evolutions inhibits the wasteland waiting to be discovered and tamed! 
[*][Items] More than 15 New Armor sets to collect! Collect materials from all over Ethia to craft and create to mix and match your best look in game!
[*][INPC] A few new NPCs has join in the fray, can you find out who?
[*][Items] New lootdrops, treasures and other items has been added as part of the desert content update
[*][Quest] Some new side quests has been added, meet the townsfolk of Vokka Town and adventure with them as you progress in your journey.
[*][Tutorials] With the feedback we received previously, we have updated our questline and made our tutorials slightly more interactive.
[*][Multiplayer] Multiplayer has been in full rework mode to make the co-op up and running, a new way to connect and better connectivity between players are made.
[/list]

We have made multiple reworks with this current major patch and a lot has been targetted to help players feel more interactive with the game. A more detailed write up of that and the current patch guides will be coming soon!

As a final note, we like to thank all our supporters and backers for helping out and playing our game. Whether its the early access or the beta branch that was recently launched, we really appreciate the love and care you guys provide us. Although still in early access, we are more step further into making Re:Legend the game we want and love!!

notes.title: Magnus Lore Reveal #13 Seacolt
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34489002/dc1130f686257b8b933170908b46e5c299ed8836.png[/img]

Throughout Ethia, shooting stars are seen as a sign of good luck and prosperity, however uniquely on Vokka Island, shooting stars are seen as a sign of a new Seacolt’s birth. Looking at the star-firing powers of the Seacolt, it wouldn’t be a stretch to put two and two together. Though the Library seriously doubts the veracity of the local folklore, certainly stranger things have happened throughout Ethia’s history to outright disregard the claim.

Thorough research has been done to determine what the star-like projectiles shot from the Seacolts are consists of, however no conclusive results can be determined by the members of the Library. From what we can gather, the stars are simply light magics that are manipulated to look like star shape. Why the Seacolt would do such a thing is another mystery that seems to elude all of us here in the Library.

Library records of archeological finds of ancient structures depicts strange imagery of creatures that look very similar to Seagasus’ being ridden into war. Many Librarians suspect that these findings depict the Old War before the destruction of the World Tree. If that were to be true, then Seacolts could be the descendants of these ancient creatures, which would fundamentally alter our understanding of the origins of the Magnus.

Head Librarian,
Figaro

notes.title: Beta Branch for Multiplayer Rework is out!
notes.notes:
Greetings Tamers, today we are pleased to roll out our beta branch for Multiplayer Testing! The purpose of this test is to allow us to further sharpen the progress we have been working on and also to allow our tamers to try it out first hand before the big patch.

The main focus currently is to ensure that the multiplayer is much more stable than the release of early access and most of the work will be focused upon it.

We like to thank you all for the support and feedback you provided as well during this period.

Back to the beta branch, if you are keen on trying out the beta build please know that it is a work in progress and we will continue to work on it as you play. If you prefer for a more stable and polished experience it is suggested to wait for the official release which is around Christmas time.

Steps to join into the beta branch : 
[olist]
[*]Ensure you are logged in to your STEAM account ( You will need to have Re:Legend in your library)
[*]Look for Re:Legend in your library and right click to open the “Properties” tab.
[*]A window should pop up, look and select “betas”.
[*]In the betas tab, enter “ MULTIPLAYERTESTING ” into the code section and click “Check Code”.
[*]It should appear that the code is correct and the testing branch should be unlocked.
[*]Above the code checker, open the drop down menu and select “MP_Rework”.
[*]Once it is selected, your Re:Legend game should be downloading the beta branch.
[*]When it is done, just hit play and you should go into the beta’s game version.
[*]To go back to the original just repeat Step 6 and choose “opt out of all beta branches”.
[/olist]

We will be releasing information about the new multiplayer features soon to help out people in need, in the meantime progressing the quest as normal will be required to play in multiplayer.

PSA : It is recommended that you start a new save file when entering the beta branch. As there are a lot of work done within the system to fix major bugs that was happening throughout the game, save files of old might cause the previous bugs to remain. We advise all tamers to start fresh and if there are any bugs still, it will be much much easier to tackle in the future.

Good luck and happy taming everyone!

notes.title: Magnus Lore Reveal #12 Shroomie
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34489002/ebc88459bfee61e28c0f57cb35554b510c2fe5d5.png[/img]

Foraging is an integral part of the Zan’s way of life, having lived in communion with the other denizens of the Wilkwoods, they refrain from cultivating and destroying the forest’s land for farming. Ask any denizen about foraging and the first piece of advice would be to spot and avoid Shroomies at all cost. Not only will the Shroomies attack you if you pick them up, they also have highly poisonous spores that can debilitate a grown goblin without issue.

Shroomies play an important role as decomposers of the Forest, eating fallen branches, rotting wood and other loose plant matter. They keep the forest clean while sustaining themselves and growing to enormous sizes. One strange observation was the collection of mushrooms by some Shroomus, they don’t seem to consume the mushrooms which begs the question of why collect them in the first place. 

Fully mature Shroomies diverge into two unique lines, one being the large green Shroomas that sport multiple fungi on its cap, and the other being the red and spiky Shroomo. Local foragers would normally track Shroomas to collect mushrooms from their cap, the magnus does not seem to mind and the collected mushrooms would normally have excellent healing properties due to feeding from the Shrooma. Avoid the Shroomo at all costs, it wouldn’t be difficult to spot their bright red cap, and the spikes should be warning enough.

Head Librarian,
Figaro

notes.title: Magnus Lore Reveal #11 Pruni
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34489002/bc927c8b6f3deb0246fa259d97c48124c69cec14.png[/img]

Vokka Island is home to many natural cave systems and subterranean tunnels, from which a bounty of minerals and metals may be mined and extracted. Any interested parties however should be beware of the local magnus populations that call these habitats as home. One of these are the Prunis, a crustacean like magnus that has the ability to release shocking electrical waves against its unfortunate foes.

In the Southwestern corner of Vokka Island, you would find a cave that has the Pruni as its namesake. Home of the illustrious Prunperor, the Prunis guard it with aggresive ferocity, flinging bolts of electric at any unsuspecting intruder. Any brave souls that are foolhardy enough to attack a Prunperor would need to look out for its large area electrical attacks. I would personally recommend all to avoid approaching the Pruni Cave area, unless you like to get shocked.

According to ancient naturalist, Hallum Arcturcus Novus, he proposes that the Prunis and Blips come from a common ancestor but diverged due to the environmental conditions of each’s preferred habitat. Though the Library is unable to prove (or disprove) the claim, it is certainly uncanny how similar both the Blips and Prunis looks in terms of body shape and social structure.

Head Librarian,
Figaro 

P.S. Wear rubber boots. I repeat, wear rubber boots.

notes.title: Magnus Lore Reveal #10 Brattus
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34489002/30029b2f9a1de070bb8295412bb98f59e364ebb2.png[/img]

Under the dense canopy of the Wilkwoods, the constant pitter-patter of tiny hooves on the  ground vegetation are the tell tale signs of the presence of a group of Brattus. When one first looks upon the creature, it would not be surprising to find them incredibly cute, but behind those googly eyes hides one of the most ferocious carnivores in Ethia. The Brattus will generally hunt in packs, chasing down prey that are often many times bigger than themselves.

A newborn Brattus is born with a sizable horn compared to its body, this makes it difficult for their young legs to support and move with much stability. This fosters a need for older Brattus to be caring and protective of their younger brethren, which would explain their extremely defensive nature when it comes to any threats towards the pack. The single horn in front of the Brattus’s face constantly grows throughout its life, there have been eyewitness accounts of a Brattorg with a horn twice the size of its body, but no such specimen has ever been found.

It is speculated that the Brattus were once omnivores or even herbivores, but were pushed into the circumstance where it has to consume the flesh. When venturing deep into the Wilkwoods, it is advised that one refrains from cooking meat, due not only to how its smell attracts the Brattus but also how it sends them into a frenzy. 

Head Librarian,
Figaro

notes.title: Magnus Lore Reveal #9 Puff
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34489002/119113c3b6192822fea08ba4656f153df4f6858e.png[/img]

The Puffs of Vokka Island live in a herd-like structure, with each stage of a Puff’s maturity lending a different role that it plays for the herd. The puff starts out its life without much of the protective outer keratin layers of its older brethren, but unknown to most is the growing layer of keratin under their fur coat. Even at a young age the Puff boasts strong defensive capabilities and can withstand most attacks from the other local magnus. Despite this, the puff is extremely shy and runs away from other magnus, most likely due to them lacking outer armor.

The Kerapuff act as the defenders of the herd, running Puffs will generally seek out a Kerapuff for protection and it wouldn’t hesitate to run into danger to safeguard those of its herd. The Warpuff on the other hand are the hunters and spearhead of the Puff herd, often charging into enemies without provocation. If a Warpuff is not chasing about enemies, then it would be chasing fish and bringing them back to the herd. 

Although the Puff are not seen to be magically gifted, the curious case of their battle shout has raised much debate among the scholars of the Library. Anyone in listening range will experience a temporary madness, often citing anger and irritation for the puff that let out the shout. It is suspected that the Puff has an innate magical aptitude that is released during these shouts. One should be wary of this, since the puffs can take a lot of punishment from us but not the other way.

Head Librarian,
Figaro

notes.title: Halloween Update : Rise of the Shadow Isle
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34489002/808dcc9039dd014baebf2455157e818fbb73257f.png[/img]

The Shadow Isle, they called it. Rumors said that this island only appears on certain time of the year, and many brave adventurers who venture forth..never returned...and no one knows whats going on and whats on that island… or how long will it stay there. The first time it emerged was 150 years ago, but then it vanished after a short time. I wonder what is going on now...

I still remember when I was a child, The Great Librarian, Astheon once told me that fishermen have reported seeing shadows lurking around the shore, but due to the misty environment, it is hard to determine what are those. But it seems to be a clash between two dimensions that created such a distorted island. So, there might be treasures beyond our imagination.

I’ve warned you adventurer, don’t get close to the Shadow Isle unprepared. Great reward comes great sacrifices...

Head Librarian,
Figaro

notes.title: Magnus Lore Reveal #8 Bushwacker
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34489002/16695da04694ab8b2626b795e4ad6980cbff83a3.png[/img]

Although not much is known about the sentience of the Magnus, there certainly is irrefutable proof that certain species are able to think and talk at the level of other intelligent species like goblins and humans. Let us then discuss about arguably the most well known speaking magnus on Ethia, Busterina the Rockin Bushbrawler. Known throughout the Lands of Ethia as the Greatest Rockstar of the Century, she has improved much of the world’s understanding of the intelligence and capability of Magnus species.

Busterina comes from the Bushwacker line of Magnus, known for their incredibly powerful ears. Although docile in nature, the bushwacker is able to dish out incredible amounts of damage if provoked and will leave bruises on mischievous attackers. There are no known Bushwackers that are able to speak, although there are several cases of Bushbrawlers that are oritorily skilled. Magnus seem to be able to communicate with other species of Magnus, and seem to understand Bushbrawlers when they speak in the Common language, though this behaviour also seems to happen with Goblin and Human tamers.

The Bushwackers are native to the Wilkwoods, and are commonly seen in the outer, less dense part of the forest where there is more light and has a warmer environment. Basking in the sun and hopping through the forests seems like the only things they are doing apart from scouring the island for Kairoots. If you ever want to be friends with a Bushwacker or get an autograph from Busterina, remember to bring some Kairoots along and you’ll get them guaranteed.

Head Librarian,
Figaro

notes.title: Magnus Lore Reveal #7 Stubjaw
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34489002/4098283fff4794353a974b9a415b4d20d322444c.png[/img]

Snap Snap Snap, the shallows of Vokka Island are mired with the unsettling sounds of the Stubjaw, slowly snapping away at prey and predators alike. Extremely territorial, the Stubjaw takes an aggressive approach in protecting whatever it considers its own. Since the beginning, I have remained a safe distance away from the creatures, watching it snap up other creatures almost without scrutiny. Once fed, the Stubjaw will busk in the light to warm itself, older Stubjaws have larger scale surfaces that help them absorb more heat.

The Stubjaw is strictly carnivorous, stalking and ambushing prey with its impressive biting power. If were to come across any foe that it can’t simply chomp to pieces, the Stubjaw will resort to using a powerful water jet from its mouth to push away the unfortunate creature, this allows it to land another deadly barrage of fangs which would normally spell the end of its enemy. The armoured head of the Stubjaw also allows it headbutt with tremendous force without causing harm to itself, this will normally knock any foe down and make them vulnerable to attacks.

For the duration of my observations of the Stubjaw, I have kept my presence hidden and never approached any of them big or small. I would advise the same to anyone that travels to the shallows of Vokka Island, unless you are a competent warrior or a seasoned adventurer, the stubjaw will certainly leave a nasty bite mark to whoever that strays too close to its territory.

Head Librarian,
Figaro

notes.title: Magnus Lore Reveal #6 Jellybit
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34489002/0b8e8e9b14f527694be81b2fdcfb4020eefdfeb3.png[/img]

The first thing that greets you upon reaching the Wilkwoods Island would certainly be the tiny gelatinous Babybits that hop around its sandy beaches. Upon first contact, these creatures did not seem to mind me entering their territory and even allowed me to touch their squishy faces, but they do seem to have an aversion to others touching their ears. When one of the sailors was too keen with a Babybit’s ears, it released a good amount of jelly from its body and escaped while the sailor was stunned from the entire ordeal.

Further evolutions of the Babybit feature limbs and a more human like appearance. We do not know if this is done by mimicry or whether it is simply coincidental. The appearance of the star in the Jellybit is also a mystery, with no clear source it just appears when a Babybit matures. The star seems to amplify the magical abilities of the Jellybit with some if its projectiles and powers seeming to have a star like appearance.

According to local testimonies, the “scarf” of the Gumbit is actually part of the Gumbit’s body and the colors actually represent the mood and emotion felt at the time. There is a saying among the local that goes something along the lines of “Don’t approach the Red Scarfed Gumbit”. All in all, the Jellybit does not seem to be the most bombastic of the Magnus species, but they do work into an ecological niche of the Wilkwoods. Remember, cute squishy faces good, ears bad.

Head Librarian,
Figaro

notes.title: Magnus Lore Reveal #5 Starfin
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34489002/c5db8757e28a8ec9f0b5ecf29e6aac4cd4f980f4.png[/img]

The Origin of Magnus is a heavily debated topic among the denizens of the Library. Even with our extensive records and collections, there doesn’t seem to be a concrete or even unified theory to how Magnus are how they are. This is mostly due to the myriad of tales and legends that surround their creation, but also in part due to the many varieties of Magnus that are considered an anomaly to the natural world. One such anomaly are the Starfins of Vokka Island, commonly seen floating about the coastal beaches of the island.

Though the Starfin has a piscine-like appearance, it is definitely not a fish, lacking the ability to swim and most importantly breathe underwater. The Starfin can usually be observed lounging by the shallow waters, bracing against the low waves of Vokka, munching on vegetation that was brought in by the tides. Starfins, no matter at what point of their growth, are extremely shy and tend to avoid contact with other species of magnus, the sight of a Starjade running away from a Pruni is certainly the comical highlight of the expedition.

The Starfin is able to release a debilitating miasma that can slow and sometimes stun any aggressors that come uncomfortably close to its territory. This helps them create an opening to escape,however should an enemy still persist then they are able to concentrate their miasmatic magics to attack and push back foes. The Starjades have by far the best offensive ability in the family, sporting fins that are able to project strong magic forces that can slice through most defence. These creatures should be left alone to bask in the sun, make sure to not release them into water should you find one hurt.

Head Librarian,
Figaro

notes.title: Magnus Lore Reveal #4 Triemer
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34489002/cc0048a521f34ac02844879a4f2c1d6c32894618.png[/img]

Deep within the Swamps of the Wilkwoods, it is common for explorers to hear soft whirring coming from behind the trees that dot the landscape. Triemers are truly fascinating creatures, not only to behold but also to understand. It would seem that certain parts of its body are almost mechanical in nature, but how exactly such a thing can spawn naturally from the soft and fleshy Triemer is beyond the knowledge of even the Library. 

Approaching one of these Triemers is much easier than it first seemed, despite their touch and prickly appearance they are rather docile when unprovoked. One thing to be aware of is sticky goo that they leave behind, one would be lucky to leave only a shoe behind, though I have seen much worse fates that befell smaller creatures unlucky enough to meet the sticky menace. During the days after the full moon, the Swamps will be covered in Triemer slime most likely due to the races that happen between Gyramers every full moon.

It is a bad idea for anyone unprepared to attack a Triemer, although they may seem slow and an easy target, a Triemer has one of the strongest bites listed in Library records. Its hard shell also blocks against most incoming attacks, deflecting and blunting all manners of weapons. A Triemer’s drills are also able to pierce through unsuspecting assailants, possessing an uncanny ability to project attacks using the power of its spin. My official advice is to leave these gentle giants alone, it won’t bother you if you don’t do anything that bothers it.

Head Librarian,
Figaro 

P.S. Requesting additional funds for shoes.

notes.title: Magnus Lore Reveal #3 Cranite
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34489002/827b37a0ba8c240c6978a2450e6c2bd36a0f7975.png[/img]

Let’s start with this, the larger members of the Cranites are fiercely territorial, attacking anything that gets too close to their nesting areas. Which would explain why I am now shipwrecked on a desert island, surrounded by hundreds of these shelled creatures skittering about. The youngest and smallest of them are observed to be rather shy in nature, constantly avoiding other creatures that seem a threat to them. Though what creature has the ability to pierce their extremely hard shell is beyond me, perhaps they have some exploitable weakness that is not apparent but other than that there seems to be no natural predators to the Cranite.

The Cranite has a chance to go through two distinct lines of evolution, the Cragnavis or Crachium line. Both seem to have an impressive ability to burrow into the ground, this allows them to blend into their surroundings and capture prey without detection. The Cragnavis line are generally less aggressive but they travel in what almost seems like a herd, if one of them is attacked then others in the vicinity will rush to fend off the attacker together. The Crachium on the other hand are more solitary creature, prefering to comb the beaches and spear unsuspecting fish from the shallow waters.

The Cranites are an especially hardy bunch, surviving on the barest of environments and using their natural skills and ingenuity to protect one another. I would suggest that any adventurers or fortune seeker be cautious when thinking about engaging these shelled creatures, if you see an odd looking rock that looks like it can pounce on you at any moment then my advice would be to run the other way. Also if my shipwrecked vessel were not warning enough, avoid the Cranite Island unless you are truly prepared or have a death wish.

Head Librarian,
Figaro 

P.S. I don't think I can survive on this island for much longer.

notes.title: Magnus Lore Reveal #2 Nerlict
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34489002/20dd01e8401379fddaea21bb3f02f5dd7dd18fc8.png[/img]

The Unseen Terrors, the Shadow Stalkers, many names have been given to the insectoid magnus known as the Nerlict. All tales recorded and spoken were never pleasant, normally ending with fallen comrades or severe injuries or both. Thus my mission to collect information about this fearsome creature is taken with much reservation, but I am in no position to fret. The Library requires, the Librarian acquires.

The Deeper Wilkwoods are already unpleasant as it is, dark, humid, and an endless chittering that seems to be coming from all directions. The local village folk were kind enough to provide me with balms to soothe the bites of small insects, but it would provide no help should I be bitten by one of the Nerlicts. Through observation, it looks like I need not worry about being bitten, since the Nerlict much prefers to slice open their prey with their incredibly sharp claws.

I have deduced that the gems that cover the Nerlict’s body are the source of its power, as they seem to glow slightly before it does any attack or when it turns invisible. The quantity and size of the gems dictate how strong a Nerlict is, and when it gains enough gems, will evolve into the next form of its line. It would seem that the way the Nerlict bolsters its own gems is by consuming others of its kind, the ones to eat the most are always the leader of the pack until the day when another comes to return the favor. Truly terrifying creatures, I would suggest not bringing one back to the Library.

Head Librarian,
Figaro

notes.title: Magnus Lore Reveal #1 Draconewt
notes.notes:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/XNHieIl.png[/img]

Not many know of the Old Temples, and even lesser known is the one that lies deep within the remote island of Vokka. Upon walking through the crumbling entranceway, one would be greeted with the sounds of snapping jaws and squishy feet. Upon first observation, the Draconewt seems to have an affinity for the water, splashing around in puddles and playfully spraying each other with jets of water magic. The same cannot be said with the evolutions of the Draconewt, which displays a wide range elemental adaptation from the Earth Rendering Dracolem, to the Healing Light of the Dracoralth, the Draconewt shows an impressive range of physical and magical alterations between its evolutions.

The Old Tomes of the Library have an entry of these enigmatic magnus. According to ancient scholars, they were once plentiful and could be seen roaming the entire island. According to the local folklore, there is a great Draconewt that towers over all its brethren that will appear once every thousand years. There is no evidence of this creature from all my searching and gathering around Vokka Coast. Perhaps this creature never existed, or maybe it is not a natural evolution of the Draconewt.

The Draconewts appear to be friendly creatures, even when approached they do not immediately feel threatened or attack without cause. Their diet seems to have a strong effect on their eventual evolution type, more observations need to be done to determine exactly what triggers their evolutions. They truly are magnificent creatures, I wonder if I will ever be able to see the giant Dracorneus with my own eyes.

Head Librarian,
Figaro

notes.title: Re:Legend is now LIVE, a few words from us to you, and what to expect in the future patches/updates!
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34489002/b519f84e9e6b7c000fe5ab5cb71e921f2dd77c06.png[/img]

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m3q5yZg0sls
First of all, We would love to say thank you to all who supported us since day one. It was a rough but exciting journey to all of us in Magnus Games Studio and we've finally released our game on Early Access. We wanted to apologize about the bugs and multiplayer stability, we understand the frustration, and we've read through all your comments, including live streams. We will be working on fixes and patches very frequently, and we sincerely apologize on that. That is also the reason why we wanted to be in Early Access, to learn, to improve and to make Re:Legend a better game. Thanks to those who gave us an up vote, we appreciate that, In the other hand, we will work hard so we could change your down votes back up soon. Action speaks louder than words, following would be What we prepared for EA launch, Bugs we've found and collected from you guys, and what to expect in the future updates, we have a dedicated [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/823950/discussions/0/1637543304835221551/]discussion topic[/url] pinned at our steam forum too, check back from time to time and thank you for your time guys!

notes.title: Re:Legend, the monster farming sim-JRPG, is coming to Steam at the end of August
notes.notes:
Re:Legend is a "sim JRPG" inspired by games like Harvest Moon and Stardew Valley, except that instead of raising crops and farm animals, you're taming and raising monsters known as Magnus. It enjoyed a tremendously successful Kickstarter campaign in 2017 and then connected with publisher 505 Games for a planned Steam Early Access release in 2018.

These things don't always work out quite according to schedule, but 505 has now committed Re:Legend to an August 30 Early Access release on Steam. Players will awaken on Vokka Island with no memory of how they got there, and must learn to survive—farming, fishing, making friends, and occasionally fighting—while embarking on adventures to reclaim lost memories. It's playable solo, or in co-op multiplayer groups of up to four people.

Developer Magnus Games Studio described the Early Access release as the final phase of Re:Legend's development, but a full release isn't quite imminent. The Early Access period is expected to last 9-12 months, during which time players can "help the development team define the final game content." The game world will also be expanded with new biomes throughout the Early Access phase.

Re:Legend is currently available for wishlisting, and will go for $20 when the Early Access release is live. Hit up play-relegend.com to find out more.
